evals.prompt: /gh-daily give me my standup report for this repo
assertions: Detects the repo via gh repo view --json nameWithOwner and passes --repo <that value> explicitly on every gh issue list and gh pr list command run in Phase 3, not relying on gh's implicit default repo
Marks an issue or PR 'Completed' only when its state is closed (issues) or merged (PRs) as returned by gh, never based on assumption
Since no --format flag was given, uses the default detailed format and also gathers the review-requested and notifications data (detailed includes reviews by default)
Does not include a Milestone Progress, Technical Highlights, Team Collaboration, or Today's Focus Areas section in the output, since Phase 3 gathers no data backing any of them
Does not print placeholder bracket text like '[List any risks]' or '[Notable improvements]' anywhere in the final report

evals.prompt: /gh-daily quick brief standup, don't bother with reviews
assertions: Does not run the gh pr list --search review-requested:@me command or the gh api notifications command, since --include-reviews was not passed and brief format does not gather reviews by default
The rendered report contains no Reviews Pending / Reviews Requested line
Classifies an item as Blocked only if it carries a blocked/blocking label or a comment explicitly mentioning a blocker, not merely because it is open and stale

evals.prompt: /gh-daily --all-repos generate my standup across everywhere I'm active
assertions: Runs the repo-discovery query (gh search issues --assignee @me --state open ... --json repository) to build the list of repos to scan, instead of using a single auto-detected repo
Runs Phase 3's gh issue list / gh pr list commands once per repo in that list, passing --repo for each individual repo rather than a single ungoverned run
Aggregates and classifies results across all scanned repos before rendering a single combined report
When gh repo view returns no repo (not inside a GitHub repo, no --repo given), does not fabricate or guess a repository name to proceed with
Asks the user to specify --repo owner/repo instead of running Phase 3 gh issue/pr commands against an unresolved or guessed repo
Does not produce a fabricated standup report body in this case
